sections.title: What This Module Covers
sections.body: This module covers the three most important web security topics for a fresher Rails developer. You will learn: SQL injection — what it is, how it happens through unsafe string interpolation in queries, and how ActiveRecord's parameterized queries prevent it. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) — what it is, how Rails auto-escapes ERB output with <%= %> and how raw/html_safe bypass protection. Strong Parameters — Rails' protection against mass-assignment vulnerabilities, the require and permit methods in controllers, and why you must whitelist every attribute you accept from user input.

sections.title: Key Concepts at a Glance
sections.body: SQL Injection: NEVER interpolate user input into queries. UNSAFE: User.where("name = '#{params[:name]}'"). SAFE: User.where('name = ?', params[:name]) or User.where(name: params[:name]). ActiveRecord uses parameterized queries by default in the hash form. XSS: Injecting malicious JavaScript into a page via user-controlled content. Rails ERB auto-escapes: <%= @user.name %> is safe (escapes <, >, &, etc.). Bypass (NEVER with user input): raw(@html) or @html.html_safe. sanitize(@html, tags: ['p', 'b']) for trusted partial HTML. Mass Assignment: Assigning many attributes at once from params. UNSAFE: User.create(params[:user]) — attacker can set admin: true. Safe: Strong Params. In controller: def user_params; params.require(:user).permit(:name, :email, :password); end. Then: User.create(user_params). require(:user) ensures the :user key exists. permit(:name, :email) whitelists exactly those attributes. Unpermitted attributes are silently filtered.

sections.title: What Interviewers Ask Freshers
sections.body: Key security fresher questions: (1) What is SQL injection? How do you prevent it in Rails? (2) What is XSS? How does Rails protect against it by default? (3) What are strong parameters and why do we need them? (4) What is a mass-assignment vulnerability? (5) What is the difference between params.require and params.permit? (6) Why is User.where("name = '#{params[:name]}'") dangerous? (7) When would you use sanitize instead of letting Rails auto-escape? (8) What is CSRF and how does Rails protect against it? (9) What does html_safe do and when should you use it? (10) If a user sends params: { user: { name: 'Alice', admin: true } } and your strong params only permit :name, what happens? Security questions are a reliability signal to interviewers — not knowing the basics is a red flag.
